issues.title: Boundary-penalty estimate loses the lowest-order convergence guarantee
issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims a flux contribution h^(2r)||u||_(H^r)^2 in the squared mesh-dependent error norm, including nonempty flux boundaries Gamma_u. For e=u-Pi_(d,h)u, the norm contains gamma h^(-1)||e.n||_(Gamma_u)^2. The cut-trace bound and the interpolation estimates used by the proof instead give O(h^(2r-2))||u||_(H^r)^2. At full regularity r=k_u+1 this becomes h^(2k_u). The paper explicitly allows and uses k_u=k_p=0, for which the supported term is O(1), not a decaying error bound. This establishes failure of the supplied proof to support the advertised convergence theorem, not a counterexample to numerical convergence. The boundary loss is absent when Gamma_u is empty.
issues.overall_effect: For nonempty flux boundaries the supported correction loses one power of h in the norm. In the lowest-order Raviart-Thomas regime it removes the convergence guarantee in that norm altogether. Higher-order Raviart-Thomas bounds remain suboptimal but convergent; the pure-pressure case is unaffected, and the BDM pair retains its overall optimal order because k_u=k_p+1. The associated optimal-convergence prose needs the same qualification.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a boundary-dependent flux estimate: retain h^(2r)||u||_(H^r)^2 when Gamma_u is empty and use h^(2r-2)||u||_(H^r)^2 for nonempty Gamma_u and r>=1. At full regularity this is the v2 factor h^(2(k_u+alpha)), with alpha=1 for pure pressure and alpha=0 otherwise. Qualify the optimal-convergence prose and explicitly withdraw the lowest-order Raviart-Thomas convergence guarantee in the affected boundary regime. The author's v2 theorem additionally uses stronger full-regularity assumptions and ||u||_(H^(k_p+2)) for the divergence contribution; its whole revision is not merely an exponent edit. Its report that the suboptimality was not observed numerically does not recover the missing proved guarantee.
issues.why_classification: Although the supported trace/interpolation correction is contained, its mathematical loss is major in a natural explicitly included regime: the bound ceases to decay for lowest-order Raviart-Thomas elements with a flux boundary. No verified complete alternative preserving convergence there has been identified. Serious reflects this loss, not a claim that every conceivable repair requires a new proof architecture or that sharper estimates can never exist. A one-order rate loss alone is not the general reason for serious severity.
